Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Contents 1 Overview 2 Action phase 2.1 Types of actions (2 AP per turn) 2.2 Card play 2.3 Hex properties 3 Clean-up phase Overview Rivals is a deckbuilding board game based on a Battle Royale gameplay. You play the chosen one of your clan and fight to save your people from extinction. You win by being the last man standing or collecting 5 Rival Points (RP). You collect Rivals Points by eliminating players, spending ressources or by negotiating with Sponsors. The game is played over 3 Eras, which consist of a speficic amount of rounds. Each round consists of the action phase and clean-up phase. The active player is changing clockwise and players have two turns with 2 action points (AP) each action phase/round. During the first turn of the first action phase no attack cards are allowed to play. Action phase Types of actions (2 AP per turn) Scout (0 AP): turn over any adjacent tiles (can be repeated) Move (1 AP): Move 2 spaces (other Ashak do not block, cannot be interrupted) Collect (1 AP): Collect All resources of the tile + bonus of the space (tile is drained for 2 rounds) Negotiate (1 AP): Pay 1 Anticipation Token (AT) → Gain 1 RP + choose additional reward → sponsor is removed afterwards Install 1 schema gain 2 AT uninstall 2 cards (hand/discard) Spend ressources (0 AP): Shield: Pay 2 Resin → Shield on field (max. 2 per player) → blocks 1. shot of salvo → destroys Uninstall: Pay 2 Crystal → Uninstall 1 card, draw new card Install: Pay 5 resources of one kind (resin or crystal) → Install 1 schema Rivals Point: Pay 10 ressources of one kind (resin or crystal) → 1 RP Whenever you install cards, they go straight to your hand. [Rating: 1/10] Mistakes in rulebook and poor iconography make learning this game a nightmare. Just finding the starting player cards in the deck are different as there is inconsistent design to note what cards go with which player. I never got to actually playing the game because I spent 45 minutes sorting cards and trying to finish the setup steps.

[Rating: 2/10] Didn’t know what to do after reading the rulebook back to front and back. Very bad written rulebook that is. Then we decided to play and look up rules as we go, that didn’t turn out a great idea. Still have no idea what I played and what we were supposed to do.

[Rating: 3/10] This game has all the ingredients of what could become a good game if development had been completed. What it’s now is a beautifully produced boring tedious repetitious game, which is weird because you would expect more tension in a confrontational game like this. If you are interested in would wait, I expect the second hand market will be flooded with cheap copies soon. Best strategy: keep away from opponents and keep harvesting.

[Rating: 4/10] Got the Legends edition and overall this game is just mid. I'm sure it's a great idea and feels fun to play as the creators of the game, but it just doesn't translate as a new player. It is super fiddly and I feel like I constantly have to look up info and house rule stuff because the rulebook lacks a lot of info. Hard to understand all the cards and hard to know how to properly even set up characters, as they didn't include it in the rulebook. The Legends edition doesn't have different types of sleeves as advertised in the Kickstarter. There are also no square sleeves included for some cards.

[Rating: 4/10] So many turns where had to pass without doing anything b/c didn't have the right cards... board layout kept changing and took a lot of damage, but was able to refill 2HP each turn if started on a lake, but then at the end down to both of us on a single hex, so only cards with range 0 could do anything and it was a volcano so I wasn't healing - I had 14HP to start and slowly lost it all, had poison and couldn't do anything about it, kept having to pass having done nothing on my turn, so frustrating.  #LetterR #Head-to-Head #Battle #Water #Lakes #Weapons #BGA

[Rating: 6/10] Battle Royale type of game, where you either rush for the 5 points or be last standing. I think game has some interesting elements and varied strategies, game is fine and works for what it is, but for me personally it felt a bit slog-ish, but overall I do not think it is my type of game.

[Rating: 7/10] Fun game, will definitely create some disputes within the group since you could interpret rules in multiple ways (pretty much like all board games). The revised rule book that the developers published is a must i would say, so make sure you use this.  A bit bummed that they didn't decide to reprint cards that was identified with errors. It's hard to keep track of all cards when you play so would have been better to have them reprinted than a new rule book with just the explanation of which cards that have been miss printed.

[Rating: 7/10] After 2 plays at 2 and 4 players, I'd say this game is fun but I would cautiously recommend it. Certain things get a bit lost in translation, both due to the literal translation from French and convoluted rules. Some of the abilities and general rules make sense once you understand the flow of the game, but is written in a really strange way.   Ultimately, your experience will depend on your enjoyment of PVP and knock out games, the good and bad are both present here.   If you are interested in trying out this battle royale, consider joining their official discord for rules clarifications.
